GER 155.heading: GER155
GER 155.name: Critical Artificial Intelligence
GER 155.summary: Studies the history and theory of artificial intelligence through humanities analysis, including how machine-learning systems are constructed and their philosophical, political and cultural implications.

C LIT 155.heading: C LIT155
C LIT 155.name: Critical Artificial Intelligence
C LIT 155.summary: Studies the history and theory of artificial intelligence through humanities analysis, including how machine-learning systems are constructed and their philosophical, political and cultural implications.

CMPSC 25.heading: CMPSC25
CMPSC 25.name: Data Programming and Analytics for Artificial Intelligence
CMPSC 25.summary: Develops Python programming and data-analysis workflows for AI, covering acquisition, cleaning, transformation, simulation, visualization and statistical inference through projects.
CMPSC 25.prerequisites: CMPSC 9 or CMPSC 24 with a grade of C or better; and, Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).

CMPSC 41.heading: CMPSC41
CMPSC 41.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
CMPSC 41.summary: Introduces discrete mathematics through counting, sets, graph theory, elementary probability and number theory.
CMPSC 41.prerequisites: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.

CMPSC 42.heading: CMPSC42
CMPSC 42.name: Logic and Automata
CMPSC 42.summary: Introduces propositional and predicate logic alongside formal languages, automata and Turing-machine models of computation.
CMPSC 42.prerequisites: Computer Science 41; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.

CMPSC 135.heading: CMPSC135
CMPSC 135.name: Mathematics of Artificial Intelligence
CMPSC 135.summary: Develops statistical, linear-algebra and optimization foundations for AI, including estimation, graph probability models, gradient methods, convex optimization, kernels and backpropagation.
CMPSC 135.prerequisites: Math 4A; CMPSC 25 or CMPSC 24; and ECE 139.

CMPSC 183.heading: CMPSC183
CMPSC 183.name: Ethics, Privacy, Fairness, and Bias in AI and Computing
CMPSC 183.summary: Examines responsible AI through privacy, bias, fairness, transparency and human oversight, using case studies and practical cloud tools for explainability and model monitoring.

CMPSC 187.heading: CMPSC187
CMPSC 187.name: Deep Learning
CMPSC 187.summary: Studies deep-learning principles, convolutional/recurrent/Transformer/graph architectures, loss design, training and inference with analysis and implementation.

CMPSC 184.heading: CMPSC184
CMPSC 184.name: Mobile Application Development
CMPSC 184.summary: Develops and deploys mobile applications using software design, development practices and testing tools.
CMPSC 184.prerequisites: Computer Science 56 or Computer Science 156; and Computer Science 130A.

CMPSC 153A.heading: CMPSC153A
CMPSC 153A.name: Hardware/Software Interface
CMPSC 153A.summary: Designs embedded software under real-time and resource constraints, using I/O protocols, interrupts and static/dynamic scheduling.
CMPSC 153A.prerequisites: Upper division standing in Computer Science, ComputerEngineering, or Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.

CMPSC 181.heading: CMPSC181
CMPSC 181.name: Introduction to Computer Vision
CMPSC 181.summary: Studies computer-vision methods for images and video, including segmentation, pattern recognition, motion, stereo, shape recovery and object recognition.
CMPSC 181.prerequisites: Upper-division standing in Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

ECE 139.heading: ECE139
ECE 139.name: Probability and Statistics
ECE 139.summary: Introduces probability and statistics, including conditional probability, Bayes rules, random variables, moments, Markov chains and hypothesis testing.
ECE 139.prerequisites: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only.

ECE 153A.heading: ECE153A
ECE 153A.name: Hardware/Software Interface
ECE 153A.summary: Designs embedded software under real-time and resource constraints, using I/O protocols, interrupts and static/dynamic scheduling.
ECE 153A.prerequisites: Upper division standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science and Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.

ECE 180.heading: ECE180
ECE 180.name: INTRODUCTION TO DEEP LEARNING
ECE 180.summary: Introduces multilayer neural networks, perceptrons, associative memory, backpropagation, convolutional/recurrent networks and attention, with language and vision applications.
ECE 180.prerequisites: Open to EE, Computer Engineering and Computer Science with upper-division standing.

ECE 181.heading: ECE181
ECE 181.name: Introduction to Computer Vision
ECE 181.summary: Studies computer-vision methods for images and video, including segmentation, pattern recognition, motion, stereo, shape recovery and object recognition.
ECE 181.prerequisites: Upper-division standing in Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

ECE 186.heading: ECE186
ECE 186.name: Probabilistic Machine Learning
ECE 186.summary: Develops probabilistic machine-learning methods, including regression, inference, estimation, Markov models, expectation maximization and reinforcement learning, with implementation projects.

ME 107.heading: ME107
ME 107.name: Machine Learning
ME 107.summary: Formulates and implements machine-learning problems in Python, covering generalization, optimization, principal components, regression, support-vector machines and neural networks.
ME 107.prerequisites: ME 17; or consent of instructor Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): PSTAT 120A.

CMPSC 1A.heading: CMPSC1A
CMPSC 1A.name: Artificial Intelligence Seminar
CMPSC 1A.summary: Introduces foundational AI techniques and interdisciplinary applications through faculty seminars, readings and discussion.

WRIT 109ES.heading: WRIT109ES
WRIT 109ES.name: Writing for Environmental Studies
WRIT 109ES.summary: Analyzes and practices professional environmental writing, emphasizing audience, research, document design, collaboration and editing for topics such as water management and sustainability.
WRIT 109ES.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Not open for credit after English 109I.
